SMTO-JOB-0003 — Another job is still using what this step needs

GUID: a18935b0-7763-47d9-a372-485cb0b024bb
Slug: job-conflict
Domain: JOB · Subsystem: job

What happened

  • SMTO didn't run this step because a background job from this task is still working on the same files or resources. Running both at once could make them interfere.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait for the earlier background job to finish. While it runs, the conversation shows Background job remains active. Once that job finishes, the files or resources it was using are free for this step.
  2. Open Inspect execution in the conversation to see the job's status and latest output. This shows whether the job is still making progress or looks stuck.
  3. If the job is stuck or no longer needed, ask SMTO to stop it, then check what it already changed before letting SMTO continue. A stopped job may have done part of its work, and this step should start from what is really there.

What success looks like

  • The earlier job finishes or is stopped, and this step runs and shows its output.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't run the same command by hand on that computer while the earlier job is still running.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A foreground shell, Python or workspace operation was not started because active non-read jobs in this run hold overlapping resources (conflicting_jobs).

What this means

  • Before a foreground shell/Python operation, conflicting_jobs returns existing job owners of overlapping resources. Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.

Why this can happen

  • Before a foreground shell/Python operation, conflicting_jobs returns existing job owners of overlapping resources.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the returned job IDs and job_control_unavailable flag; an unavailable observation may require reconciliation rather than waiting blindly.

How to fix it

  • execute_operation returned resource_busy with job_conflict and the blocking job_ids; the conflict blocked it before it started. Wait for, inspect or cancel those jobs with manage_job and confirm their outcome before repeating; job_control_unavailable means the Gateway could not be queried for them.
  • Inspect current job and resource ownership, then act against the latest state.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • Existing owners settle or reconcile and ordinary resource admission permits the intended operation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Job identity, supervision and dispatch/terminal receipts own effect truth. Diagnostics do not launch, cancel or replay work; missing output or failed control does not prove that the original process stopped.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
